A bunny that hops. A raccoon that reacts.

The earlier baseline version passed nine unit/server checks, seven deterministic browser checks, and all 9 live browser checks. It uses the approved R1 raccoon and B1 garden style, one log per obstacle row, and visible jumps between neighboring paths.

When speed outruns the decision loop

Each moving stage ran for 14 seconds, with 500 ms captures, 384 px screenshots, a two-request limit, and 420 px obstacle spacing. A jump takes 280 ms. “In time” requires the reply to leave room to finish that jump. Increasing game speed changes the available deadline; it does not inherently increase the API's processing time. Bumps are measured separately.

Decisions identifies the rabbit's path and nearest approaching log's path in two choice questions over the screenshot. A fixed policy keeps moving if those paths differ; if blocked, Path 1 jumps right and Paths 2 or 3 jump left. Both positions come from API answers. Local obstacle state supplies only evaluation labels and collision scoring. Earlier direct-action prompt trials were less reliable and are preserved separately; their scores are not pooled into the final result.

Live voice evidence

The local synthetic microphone fixture produced 257 input-transcript characters and 196 generated-transcript characters. Received audio: 133,578 bytes; the browser audio clock advanced 20.1 seconds. Maple changed among neutral, delighted, excited, and thoughtful during 28 live expression decisions. Voice setup took 4032 ms. The session finalized with 20 billable seconds and reason close_requested; estimated voice cost for this session was $0.0167.

This proves automated speech input, generated audio transport/playback, expression changes, and final usage. It does not substitute for human listening quality or measure microphone-to-expression latency. Voice and Decisions are different APIs.

Controls and limitations

The live app exposes speed, log spacing, capture interval, image width, concurrency, and expression refresh. Samples export as JSON and CSV. Cost reservations persist across restarts; uncertain calls retain their reservation. No automatic retries. The server keeps the key private and logs no transcript, audio, or screenshots. The $5 ledger covers this project's API calls and is an estimate, not an invoice. Built-in artwork generation is separate.

There is no current API-access blocker: both endpoints were validated with the configured key. Microphone permission and WebRTC network access are needed on each browser. Very fast settings intentionally produce late replies and collisions. Jev is deferred. Development used the local video transcript and storyboard frames; full video playback was unavailable.
